uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

packet-02 -- unverified blind image reading (first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
the work or author. The only items opened are PROMPT.md, the reader brief, and
image files in packet-02 (plus crops of them). Nothing done beyond the rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001.jpg)
- image-001 is an overview of a photo sheet with four paper fragments on black
  ground, colour checker lower left, ruler at right. Each fragment carries a
  modern pencil note "aus Einband II/6 36 (a. 1534)" and a shelf label
  "Stams, STA, Frg. 39_..." (labels seen: 4r top-left, 3r bottom-left, 2v? top
  right, 1v bottom right).
- Left two fragments (top-left, bottom-left): written faces, each an opened
  bifolium-like spread with two text blocks (left page / right page) divided by
  a vertical fold. Single column per page, about 15-17 lines each. Cursive
  late-medieval/early-modern hand in brown ink, heavy abbreviation.
- Top-left fragment, right page: heading line at top "Carin(us)? Pamphil(us)?"
  (written in a heading position), followed by a large decorated initial (H?)
  in brown ink. Bottom-left fragment, right page: heading "Pamphilus adolescens
  Davus serv(us)" (tentative) followed by a large decorated initial V. Left page
  of bottom-left fragment, near bottom: a line reading like "... ancilla.
  Pamphilus. Carinus / adolescentes. Davus servus." and below that another
  decorated initial. These look like speaker-name headings with initials
  marking new sections (observation; interpretation tentative).
- Right two fragments: largely blank or faint faces. Top-right shows some lines
  of a later(?) cursive, apparently German, in the right half; bottom-right
  appears nearly blank with faint traces.
- No interlinear or marginal glosses seen at overview scale.

Tiles: image-002..010 appear to be a 3x3 tiling of the image-001 sheet at
native resolution (rows: 002-004 top, 005-007 middle, 008-010 bottom).
image-011/021/031 are further overviews, each followed by 9 tiles.
